subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria, and grading rubric
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria, and grading rubric

Thanks for the call today - great alignment overall. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed evaluation plan and success criteria so we can move quickly on the POC. Please review and flag anything missing; if this looks good we'll: (1) confirm dataset access, (2) schedule a technical kickoff with Dylan, and (3) start the offline eval next week.

High-level goals (what success looks like)
- Functional: model responses meet intent accuracy and extraction quality for the 1st-line support use case. Target: weighted quality score >= 0.80 (see rubric attached).
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 400ms for median request size (typical prompt ~250 tokens).
- Safety/Integrity: low hallucination rate (<5% of sampled responses) and no PII leakage during the eval windows.
- Ops: integration-ready with clear logging/traceability and reproducible prompts.

Proposed evaluation approach
1) Offline (controlled) eval - primary first step (2 weeks)
   - Use a labeled test set (we discussed ~2,000 queries across top 6 intents).
   - Run batch generation; score against gold labels and rubric (accuracy, rouge/EM where relevant, hallucination flagging).
   - Ownership: Marissa (overall PM), Dylan (SE lead; handles prompts & infra), Acme to provide labeled set and privacy constraints.

2) Online shadowing (1 week) - follow-up if offline looks good
   - Shadow model alongside production traffic (non-critical traffic split) to assess real-world behavior, latency under realistic load, and edge-case failure modes.
   - Ownership: Acme engineering + Redwood infra.

3) Decision gate and acceptance
   - Pass threshold: weighted score >= 0.80 AND latency & safety constraints met. Conditional if score in 0.75-0.80 with agreed remediation plan.

Timeline (target)
- Technical kickoff: within 3 business days of confirmation
- Offline eval window: 2 weeks after kickoff
- Shadowing: 1 week following successful offline eval
- Decision review: 2 business days after shadow window

Attachments: acme-poc-plan-v1.pdf (detailed schedule), acme-eval-rubric.xlsx (scoring matrix).

Next steps for Alex/Jordan:
- Confirm dataset availability and any data privacy constraints by EOD Wed 3/3
- Approve the proposed timeline or propose adjustments

Thanks - happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme POC: evaluation plan, success criteria, and grading rubric

Thanks Alex - good questions. Looping Dylan (SE) and Rachel (CS) so they can own technical kickoff and success tracking. Answers below plus a more explicit grading rubric excerpt so procurement/security can review.

Weighting (proposed):
- Accuracy / functional correctness: 50%
- Safety / hallucination & privacy checks: 25%
- Latency / reliability: 15%
- Integration / observability readiness: 10%

Grading rubric (summary) - full spreadsheet attached (acme-eval-rubric.xlsx)
- Accuracy metrics (50%): intent accuracy, slot extraction F1 where applicable, response-level correctness. Score computed as weighted average of these submetrics.
- Safety (25%): sample 200 responses for safety review (policy violations, hallucinations, PII leakage). Each violation deducts points; pass threshold is <5% violations.
- Latency (15%): 95p < 400ms = full points; linear deductions up to 800ms.
- Integration (10%): logging, trace ids in responses, predictable tokenization/cost estimates.

Decision logic: final weighted score >=0.80 = Pass. 0.75-0.80 = Conditional (requires remediation plan & second pass). <0.75 = Fail. Safety or privacy failures (e.g., PII leakage) are immediate fail regardless of score.

Data/privacy: understood. Jordan - could you confirm whether you can provide an anonymized export of historical interactions to use as the labeled set, or whether we should plan to synthesize to avoid any PII handoff? Redwood can run local-only offline evaluation in your VPC if that helps (we can provide a script that runs inside your environment and returns only aggregate metrics).

Next steps (owners):
- Jordan (Acme): confirm data approach by EOD Wed 3/3
- Dylan (Redwood SE): schedule tech kickoff and request sample prompts + schema
- Rachel (Redwood CS): prepare acceptance checklist and shared dashboard link for results
- Marissa: coordinate decision meeting and procurement readiness

Dylan - can you suggest 60-90 minute slots for kickoff?

Best,
Marissa
